newsitem.title: INDIA: India agrees to talks with Pakistan this month.
newsitem.headline: India agrees to talks with Pakistan this month.

text.p: India has agreed to resume talks with Pakistan at the level of senior officials later this month, the United News of India (UNI) reported on Saturday.

"I believe that we have a real opportunity to bring a new spirit into our relations and to create an environment for cooperation," it quoted Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral as saying in a letter to his Pakistani counterpart Gohar Ayub Khan.
Pakistan said earlier on Saturday it hoped for an early resumption of stalled peace talks with India and was willing to discuss a troop pullout from a disputed Himalayan glacier.

A Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokesman told reporters that Islamabad wanted a peaceful negotiated settlement of problems and "honestly believes in normal good-neighbourly relations" between the two countries, which have fought three wars since their independence from Britain in 1947.
"We hope that the response from India will be positive and it will be possible to resume these negotiations at an early date," the spokesman said.

Gujral told the Press Trust of India news agency earlier on Saturday there had been a big improvement in India's relationship with neighbours Bangladesh and Nepal, and that things were moving in the right direction with Pakistan.

Pakistan's new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif proposed in a recent letter to Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda that foreign ministry secretaries of the two countries meet before the end of March to "prepare the ground for meaningful discussions" between the two prime ministers.

The letter responded to one sent by Deve Gowda on February 17 congratulating Sharif on taking office, and proposing a resumption of talks on a wide range of issues, including the disputed Himalayan region of Jammu and Kashmir. India controls two-thirds of the region and Pakistan the rest.
"We were glad to receive the reply (from Sharif) in which it is suggested that the two foreign secretaries may meet in the month of March," Gujral wrote to Khan.
Gujral said he hoped to hold talks with Khan at a meeting of Non-Aligned foreign ministers in New Delhi in April. REUTER
